title: Zions Bank Helps Utah Small Businesses Thrive as Top SBA 7(a) Lender in 2025
summary: For the 29th time over the past 32 years, Zions Bank ranked No. 1 in SBA 7(a) loan approvals in the Utah District
body_markdown:
SALT LAKE CITY, Utah; Dec. 2, 2025 — In a year marked by cautious optimism and renewed entrepreneurial momentum, Utah small businesses are proving their staying power and seizing opportunities to expand with support from top SBA lender Zions Bank.


Zions Bank approved 264 U.S. Small Business Administration 7(a) loans totaling more than $40 million in the Utah District during the fiscal year ending Sept. 30, 2025, according to data from the SBA’s Utah District Office. This marks a continued upward trend in lending volume and underscores the bank’s commitment to fueling small business growth across the state.


For the 29th time over the past 32 years, Zions Bank ranked No. 1 in SBA 7(a) loan approvals in the Utah District, helping entrepreneurs access capital to launch new ventures, expand operations and invest in their communities. The average loan size was $153,267, demonstrating the bank’s support to Utah’s mom-and-pop shops, solo entrepreneurs and early-stage ventures that are critical to the state’s economy.


“Small businesses are the heartbeat of Utah’s economy, where 99% of businesses are considered small businesses,” said Tom Morgan, Zions Bank executive vice president of Retail, Business and Omnichannel Banking. “We’re honored to support them as they innovate, create jobs and build a brighter future for our state.”


In 2025, Zions Bank-supported businesses created 672 new jobs and retained 1,262 existing positions, according to SBA data. The bank’s approved loans accounted for nearly 20% of the 7(a) loans issued in the Utah District this fiscal year.


Zions Bank continues to champion inclusive entrepreneurship, with at least 30% of its SBA 7(a) loans in the Utah District awarded to businesses owned by women and people of color.


**About the SBA 7(a) Loan Program**


The 7(a) loan program is the SBA's primary program for providing financial assistance to small businesses and offers guarantees on loans to small businesses of up to $5 million on reasonable terms and conditions. These loans are commonly used for acquiring land, purchasing equipment or working capital. Credit approval required; terms and conditions apply.


**About Zions Bank**


Zions Bank is Utah’s oldest financial institution and is the only local bank with a statewide distribution of branches operating 93 full-service branches. Zions Bank also operates 26 branches in Idaho and Wyoming. In addition to offering a wide range of traditional banking services, Zions Bank is also a leader in small business lending. Founded in 1873, Zions Bank has been serving the communities of Utah for more than 150 years. Additional information is available at www.zionsbank.com.
